Az Apple Liquid Glass az iOS 26 / iPadOS 26 / macOS Tahoe 26 megjelenésével debütált, és azóta rengeteg párhuzamos kutatási és opensource implementáció foglalkozik a renderelési technikájával. Alább összefoglalom az összes lényeges réteget: a dizájnfilozófiától a fizikai optikaig és a nyílt forráskódú megvalósításokig.

 Mi az a Liquid Glass?

Az Apple az WWDC 2025ön mutatta be a Liquid Glass dizájnnyelvet, amelyet Alan Dye, az Apple humán interfész tervező alelnöke „valaha volt legátfogóbb dizájnfrissítésünknek" nevezett . Az iOS 7 óta (2013) ez az első valóban rendszerszintű vizuális újragondolás, és az első olyan dizájn, amely egységesen terjed ki az összes Apple platformra: iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe 26, watchOS 26 és tvOS 26ra . A hatás lényege, hogy az interfész elemei — gombok, tabsávok, oldalsávok, navigációs sávok — valódi üveg optikai viselkedését imitálják: fényt törnek, visszavernek és a mögöttük lévő tartalomhoz dinamikusan alkalmazkodnak .

A Liquid Glass erősen merít a visionOS féláttetsző felhasználói felületéből és az iPhone Dynamic Island folyékony animációiból . macOS Tahoeban az alkalmazások oldalsávjai és eszköztárai lebegő elemekként jelennek meg a tartalom felett, a menüsor teljesen átlátszóvá vált, a Dock pedig fagyott üveg hatást kapott . Az Apple valós idejű renderelést alkalmaz, amely mozgásra dinamikusan reagál — a hatást gombokon, csúszkákon, médiakontróllereken és teljes felületeken egyaránt alkalmazza .

 A fizika: Snelltörvény és SDF alapú refrakció

Az akadémiai és fejlesztői közösség viszonylag gyorsan feltérképezte, hogy mi zajlik a motor alatt. A kulcslépés a Snelltörvény alkalmazása: egy felületponton az üveglevegő határon megtörő fény irányát a törési szög kiszámításával kapjuk meg . A közelítés egy 2D SDF (Signed Distance Function) alapú felületleírást használ, amelyből a normálvektor automatikusan adódik az SDF gradienseként — GLSLben a dFdx / dFdy hívásokkal, majd a refract beépített függvénnyel .

A négy réteg, amelyet az Apple implementáció sűrít egyetlen shaderpassban :
 Refrakció (Snelltörvény alapján, SDF normálissal)
 Fresnelreflexió (az érintő szögeknél növekvő visszaverődés)
 Spekuláris kiemelés (multilight highlight és rimfény)
 Kromatikus aberráció (színsávosodás a peremeken, diszperzió)

Az Apple erős averziója a görbületfoly tonossághiány iránt megmutatkozik itt is: a lapos terület és a lekerekített perembevágás közötti folyamatos átmenet érdekében a n_z és a h számítási módja finomabban van kalibrálva, mint az egyszerűbb opensource megközelítésekben .

 Párhuzamos GitHub implementációk

Számos párhuzamos, nyílt forráskódú megvalósítás keletkezett, amelyek különböző technológiai utakat járnak be.

A  a webre tervezett, 4rétegű kompoziting architektúrát alkalmaz SVGalapú diszplacementmappal és CSS backdrop-filterrel . Teljesítménykapuit content-visibility: auto, contain: layout paint és isolation: isolate CSS tulajdonságokkal valósítja meg; 20+ egyidejű üvegelemmel 120 fpst ér el . Tartalmaz egy FPSGuard komponenst, amely tartósan alacsony framerate esetén automatikusan degradálja a hatást .

A  WebGL shader alapú megközelítést választott . Egy megosztott offscreen canvas segítségével kerüli meg a WebGL biztonsági korlátait, amelyek egyébként megakadályoznák a valós idejű háttérpixelek olvasását . Valós idejű refrakcióval kezeli a videót, szöveges animációkat és dinamikus tartalmat .

A  html-to-image alapú DOMraszterizálást és WebGL shadert kombinál; a statikus gyermekelemeket egyszer rögzíti és cacheeli, a data-dynamic jelölt elemeket viszont frameről framere újraraszterizálja . A renderelési hurok rövidre zár, ha semmi nem változott, ami statikus oldalakon minimális CPU terhelést jelent .

A  React Native + Expo + @shopify/react-native-skia + SkSL (Skia Shading Language) stacket használ, amely CanvasKit WASMon keresztül böngészőben is fut . Ez az egyetlen megközelítés, amely natív (iOS, Android) és webes platformon is azonos shader kóddal dolgozik . Hátránya a ~8 MBos CanvasKit WASM bináris, amely aszinkron töltést igényel .

 A webes megvalósítás alapvető korlátja

Minden implementációnak szembe kell néznie azzal, hogy a web nem biztosít natív APIt az elem mögötti renderelt pixelek lekérdezésére . Az Apple azért tudja megcsinálni, mert irányítja a teljes renderelési pipelinet: Metal shaderek, compositor, display szerver — bármely renderelt réteget textúrainputként használhatja bármelyik másik shader számára . A webfejlesztők a CSS element() (megszüntetett) és a Houdini paint worklet (korlátozott) szabványok hiánya miatt kerülőmegoldásokra kényszerülnek . A gyakorlati ajánlás ezért: backdrop-filter az általános üveges UIelemekhez, teljes shaderkezelés csak egykét kiemelt interaktív elemhez .

Apple's Liquid Glass is the company's most sweeping visual redesign since iOS 7, introduced at WWDC 2025 and shipped with iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe, and watchOS 26 in September 2025. It replaces the flat design language that had been in place since 2013 with a translucent, layered aesthetic that dynamically refracts and reflects the content beneath it.

 What It Looks Like

Liquid Glass draws direct inspiration from visionOS. Interface elements — tab bars, toolbars, navigation controls — take on a frosted, refractive quality that shifts color and luminance based on the underlying content and the user's movement. Apple described it as combining "the optical qualities of glass with a fluidity only Apple can achieve, as it transforms depending on your content or context."  In Apple Music, a droplet literally glides between sections as users tap tabs; scrolling causes background images to contort and bend behind glassy controls. The effect involves realtime rendering of specular highlights that react to motion, alongside animations where elements bounce, jiggle, and split apart during interaction. 

 The Controversy

Reception was polarizing from the start. While many users appreciated the modern, layered depth, critics — including Nielsen Norman Group — found that iOS 26 departs from established usability principles in measurable ways: shrunken tab bars, touch targets that no longer meet minimum spacing thresholds, and translucent controls that blend into visually complex backgrounds.  The Verge argued the concept works well on Vision Pro — where a layered 3D interface matches the spatial nature of a headset — but breaks down on iPhone, where every experience is fullscreen and the constant colorshifting becomes clutter rather than depth.  Apple itself quietly acknowledged some of these issues by introducing a "Tinted" glass variant after the original "Clear" option proved frequently illegible. 

 Apple's Response and Refinements

At WWDC 2026 in June, Apple announced it was "updating the foundations of how Liquid Glass is built to ensure exceptional readability," with a new technique that diffuses complex content behind glass panels to create better separation and legibility.  Crucially, Apple added a userfacing slider — ranging from "ultra clear" to "fully tinted" — so users can tune the visual intensity to their preference.  Despite the backlash, Apple made it emphatically clear at a developer workshop that Liquid Glass "is absolutely moving forward, evolving, and expanding across the ecosystem," with deferral flags in Xcode 27 being disabled, effectively making Liquid Glass mandatory for App Store apps. 

 Developer Adoption

App adoption has been uneven but accelerating. Apple built a curated developer gallery showcasing apps like Slack, CNN, OmniFocus 4, Crumbl, and AllTrails that have fully embraced the design language.  Slack treated iOS 26 as the trigger for a full app overhaul — moving search into the tab bar and gaining landscape support as a side effect. CNN redesigned its feed for edgetoedge content that flows behind translucent chrome.  More recently, the New York Times app adopted Liquid Glass in a deliberately restrained way — only applying it to the bottom tab bar and a mini audio player — reflecting how cautious publishers are about letting platform aesthetics affect editorial presentation.  Apple has reportedly set a September 2026 deadline for full Liquid Glass compatibility across App Store apps. 

 The Deeper Design Principle

The core idea behind Liquid Glass isn't just a visual style — it enforces a structural philosophy. Apple draws a distinction between the "UI layer" (navigation chrome, tab bars, toolbars) and the "content layer" (where brand, color, and voice should live). The UI layer is meant to float above content, glasslike and systemnative, while individual apps express their identity through the content below.  The most common mistake developers make is treating Liquid Glass as something to apply to every surface, rather than understanding that its job is to make navigation feel lighter and let content dominate.  This is Apple's biggest design bet in over a decade, and — like iOS 7 before it — the ecosystem is still catching up.

entries.answer: Kérlek, add meg a technikai leírást, amelyet prompt formátumba szeretnél átalakítani. A szöveg elolvasása után elkészítem a teljes, explicit, gyártásra kész promptot.

Az előző válaszomban magyarul válaszoltam, holott a feladatod angolul volt megírva — ez hiba volt. A helyes válasz:

Provide the technical description you want converted into a prompt. Once you share it, the full, explicit, productionready prompt will be produced based on its exact contents.

Build a complete, selfcontained, productionready web implementation of a translucent refractive UI effect system using HTML, CSS, SVG filters, and vanilla JavaScript (no external dependencies except optionally Anime.js for animation). The system must implement all of the following, in full, unabridged, deployable code across all required files.



Technical Description to Convert into a Prompt:



Build a complete, selfcontained, productionready web implementation of a translucent refractive UI effect system — a design language where interface elements appear to be constructed from physically plausible curved glass. The visual effect combines backdrop refraction (light bending at curved edges), specular rim lighting, chromatic aberration, optional Gaussian blur, and a semitransparent tinted overlay. Every file must be complete and unabridged.

 Architecture

The project is structured as follows. Every file listed must be delivered in full with no placeholders, no ellipses, no "// ... rest of the code" comments, and no simplified stubs.


/index.html
/style.css
/main.js
/filters.svg
/displacement-map.svg       ← procedurally defined, not a raster image
/specular-map.svg           ← procedurally defined, not a raster image


 Detailed Construction Steps

 Step 1 — displacement-map.svg

Construct an SVG displacement map for a rounded rectangle with a border-radius of 50px and fixed dimensions of 300×56 px. The map encodes perpixel displacement vectors in the red (Xaxis) and green (Yaxis) channels. The neutral value (no displacement) is #808080 (128, 128) in both channels.

The displacement map must be generated by layering the following:

1. A base fill of rgb(128, 128, 128) — neutral, no displacement.
2. A radial gradient originating from each of the four rounded corners, pushing pixels outward along both axes using redchannel values above 128 (rightward) or below 128 (leftward), and greenchannel values above 128 (downward) or below 128 (upward).
3. A blurred mask in the shape of the rounded rectangle (same border-radius) applied using feGaussianBlur with stdDeviation="6" to create a smooth transition between displaced and nondisplaced regions at the border.
4. The displacement near the border must simulate the optical behavior of a convex glass surface: pixels near the outer edge are pushed inward (toward the center), and the intensity of displacement falls to zero at the center of the element.
5. Use feComposite, feBlend, and feColorMatrix primitives inside the SVG <filter> as needed to correctly compose the layered gradients.

The resulting SVG must encode X displacement in the red channel and Y displacement in the green channel, with the blue channel fixed at 128 and the alpha channel at 255.

 Step 2 — specular-map.svg

Construct an SVG specular rim map for the same rounded rectangle (300×56 px, 50px radius). This map represents the light reflected off the glass surface.

Requirements:
1. The map is transparent everywhere except along the border of the rounded rectangle.
2. Along the border, paint a 2px stroke with a linear gradient that simulates light coming from the upperleft at approximately 135° (brighter at topleft, darker at bottomright).
3. The stroke gradient runs from rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.9) at the topleft corner to rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1) at the bottomright corner.
4. Apply feGaussianBlur with stdDeviation="1.5" to the stroke to soften it into a natural specular glow.
5. Reduce overall opacity to 55% so the highlight does not look harsh against varied backgrounds.

 Step 3 — filters.svg

Define an SVG <defs> block (hidden, display: none) containing one <filter> element with id="liquid-glass". This filter is applied via CSS backdrop-filter: url(#liquid-glass).

The filter pipeline inside <filter id="liquid-glass"> must execute the following primitives in order:

1. <feGaussianBlur in="SourceGraphic" stdDeviation="1" result="blurred_source" /> — Slight preblur of the source for smoother displacement.
2. <feImage href="./displacement-map.svg" x="0" y="0" width="300" height="56" result="displacement_map" /> — Load the displacement map.
3. <feDisplacementMap in="blurred_source" in2="displacement_map" scale="55" xChannelSelector="R" yChannelSelector="G" result="displaced" /> — Apply refraction.
4. <feColorMatrix in="displaced" type="saturate" values="3" result="displaced_saturated" /> — Increase color saturation of the displaced layer.
5. <feImage href="./specular-map.svg" x="0" y="0" width="300" height="56" result="specular_layer" /> — Load the specular rim.
6. <feGaussianBlur in="specular_layer" stdDeviation="1" result="specular_layer_blurred" /> — Soften the specular rim.
7. <feComposite in="displaced_saturated" in2="specular_layer_blurred" operator="in" result="specular_saturated" /> — Mask the saturated displaced layer by the specular rim shape.
8. <feBlend in="specular_saturated" in2="displaced" mode="screen" result="with_specular" /> — Merge specular highlight with the displaced base using screen blend.
9. <feColorMatrix in="with_specular" type="matrix" values="1 0 0.02 0 0  0 1 0 0 0  -0.02 0 1 0 0  0 0 0 1 0" result="chromatic_aberration" /> — Apply subtle chromatic aberration by shifting the red channel slightly right and the blue channel slightly left along the Xaxis.
10. Final output is chromatic_aberration.

 Step 4 — style.css

Define the following CSS rules in full:

 CSS custom properties (on :root):

--glass-width: 300px;
--glass-height: 56px;
--glass-radius: 50px;
--glass-bg: hsl(0 0% 100% / 18%);
--glass-filter: url(#liquid-glass) brightness(1.15);
--glass-border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.35);
--glass-shadow: 0 8px 32px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.18), 0 1.5px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.10);


 .glass-container:
 position: relative
 width: var(--glass-width)
 height: var(--glass-height)
 border-radius: var(--glass-radius)
 overflow: hidden
 box-shadow: var(--glass-shadow)
 cursor: pointer
 Transition on transform and box-shadow, 200ms ease

 .glass-filter-layer:
 position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: 0
 backdrop-filter: var(--glass-filter)
 isolation: isolate
 -webkit-backdrop-filter: var(--glass-filter)

 .glass-overlay:
 position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: 1
 background: var(--glass-bg)
 border-radius: inherit

 .glass-specular:
 position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: 2
 border-radius: inherit
 overflow: hidden
 box-shadow: inset 1px 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.7), inset 0 0 6px rgba(255,255,255,0.5)
 border: var(--glass-border)

 .glass-content:
 position: relative; z-index: 3
 display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center
 width: 100%; height: 100%
 font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "SF Pro Display", sans-serif
 font-size: 17px; font-weight: 600
 color: rgba(255,255,255,0.92)
 letter-spacing: -0.3px
 text-shadow: 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.25)
 user-select: none

 .glass-container:hover:
 transform: scale(1.03)
 box-shadow: 0 12px 40px rgba(0,0,0,0.22), 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.12)

 .glass-container:active:
 transform: scale(0.98)

 Safari / nonChromium fallback:
 Detect @supports not (backdrop-filter: url(#x)) and apply backdrop-filter: blur(12px) brightness(1.1) with background: hsl(0 0% 100% / 28%) as the fallback for .glass-filter-layer and .glass-overlay.

 Body and demo wrapper styles:
 Fullpage centered layout
 Animated gradient background cycling through blue, violet, and teal hues to demonstrate the glass effect against varied backgrounds
 animation: gradientShift 8s ease infinite defined with @keyframes

 Step 5 — index.html

Construct a complete HTML5 document that:

1. Includes <link rel="stylesheet" href="./style.css"> in <head>.
2. Includes <script src="./filters.svg" type="image/svg+xml"> — incorrect; instead, inlines the <svg style="display:none"> SVG filter block directly inside <body> (copy the <filter> element from filters.svg inline here).
3. Provides a demo section containing at minimum three .glass-container instances, each with the four required child layers (.glass-filter-layer, .glass-overlay, .glass-specular, .glass-content) and different label text.
4. At the bottom of <body>, includes <script src="./main.js"></script>.

 Step 6 — main.js

Write complete, nonminified JavaScript that:

1. On DOMContentLoaded, queries all .glass-container elements.
2. For each container, attaches pointerdown, pointerup, and pointerleave event listeners.
3. On pointerdown: adds a CSS class glass-pressed that reduces the --glass-filter brightness from 1.15 to 0.95 (achieved by updating a CSS custom property inline).
4. On pointerup / pointerleave: removes the class and restores the original filter value.
5. Implements a parallax tilt effect: on pointermove over a container, reads the pointer position relative to the container's bounding rect, computes X and Y tilt angles in the range [8deg, 8deg], and applies them via element.style.transform = rotateX(...) rotateY(...) scale(1.03). Resets on pointerleave.
6. Includes a resize observer that watches each .glass-container and, when the container dimensions change, updates the width and height attributes of all <feImage> elements referencing displacement-map.svg and specular-map.svg inside the inline SVG filter, as well as the width attribute of the <feDisplacementMap> element, to match the new container dimensions. This ensures the displacement and specular maps scale correctly when the container is resized.

Deliver every file listed above — index.html, style.css, main.js, filters.svg, displacement-map.svg, specular-map.svg — in full, complete, productionready code. No file may contain placeholders, stubs, ellipses, simplified sections, or any instruction to "fill in" missing parts. All SVG filter primitives must be syntactically valid and functionally correct. All CSS rules must be complete. All JavaScript must be syntactically valid, nonminified, and fully functional.
